description: Lossless bounded block. Decode every {$ref:N} from shared_values[N] (fully expanded, one lookup). quote_span_table rows: [start,end,original_quote_type,original_quote_metadata]. Each SAME-entry attached_verbatim_passage_spans_ids and answer_quotation_spans_ids references table rows in order; exact quote is full supplied summary[start:end], Unicode half-open. Original object/string metadata retained; __transport_text_field__ names text/verbatim field, remove it on restoration. Span sha256_utf8 reconstructs as SHA256 of exact quote. answer_transport joins restored answer_quotations. All original raw fields/quotes/numeric/case fields reconstruct exactly. No keys or answers outside this fixed block supplied. No cross-entry or cross-reader borrowing.

rubric.correct: Every actually requested fact correct, resolved and summary-supported; equivalent complete meaning accepted; no material contradiction.
rubric.partial: Missing/unresolved requested fact with no material contradiction.
rubric.incorrect: Any material contradiction, including volunteered contextual claims.

global_constraints: No borrowing a fact from another question or reader.
Do not require ancillary source-only facts or contextual key facts excluded here.
Named board order may convey an order without listing every suit.
A clear operational equivalent passes without parroting key wording.
Semantic relation must be present: one user is not once total; paid use is not necessarily user pays; global three Visions is not personal draws; one unmatched site card is not all unmatched.
Free Chronicle together with affirmative Exile-winner permission may convey normal-offer waiver.
This file does not certify source audit or silently fix a fixed expected answer.

questions.question: When does Narrow Pass require travel to itself or an added Campaign target, and does ruling Narrow Pass change those conditions?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Entering its region from another region must travel to Narrow Pass. Campaign declaring any targets in that region while pawn in different region must also target Narrow Pass unless attacker rules it. The rule exception applies Campaign,not generic entry; named ignore effects can override.

required_facts.expected_fact: Entering Narrow Pass region from another region must Travel to it.
Declaring targets in that region from pawn in another region requires also targeting Narrow Pass unless attacker rules it.
Rule exception applies Campaign, not ordinary entry.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Explicitly named ignore powers can override.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Generic override hierarchy is context; question asks Narrow Pass’s own conditions and rule exception.

questions.question: What must be paid to travel to Hidden Place or declare Campaign targets there, and which site powers can override this restriction?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Flip one board secret facedown;cannot travel/target there without doing so. Shrouded Wood travel ignores Hidden Place;Buried Giant ignores Narrow Pass only,not Hidden Place. Coasts ignore Narrow Pass only.
questions.source_references: Site Reference p2 Hidden Place,Shrouded Wood,Buried Giant

required_facts.expected_fact: Must flip one own-board secret facedown to Travel there or declare targets there.
Shrouded Wood Travel ignores Hidden Place.
Buried Giant/Coasts ignore Narrow Pass only, not Hidden Place.

questions.question: From Buried Giant, how can you travel without Supply, where does the secret go, and does that automatically ignore Hidden Place?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: May flip one secret on own board facedown;spend no Supply and ignore Narrow Pass when traveling from there. Secret remains board exhausted,cannot pay again before refresh. Does not name/ignore Hidden Place.
questions.source_references: Site Reference p2 Buried Giant; Law 7.1.2

required_facts.expected_fact: May flip one own-board secret facedown to spend no Supply and ignore Narrow Pass traveling from it.
Stays on board facedown/unready; cannot pay with it again until refreshed.
Not automatically ignored; power only names Narrow Pass.

questions.question: How does Marshes change Search, and does it change a remote Search simply because you rule Marshes?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Must draw one fewer if pawn there,so ordinary three becomes two,still stop at world Vision/empty source. Rule alone without pawn there does not trigger it.

required_facts.expected_fact: When pawn there, draw one fewer (ordinary three becomes two).
Ruling Marshes without pawn there does not affect Search.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Still stop at world Vision/depleted source.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Unchanged Search behavior is not an extra required part of how Marshes changes count/access.

questions.semantic_notes: Assess the stated requested rule in context; no exact-keyword demand, confidence-label grading, or borrowing from another answer. A pawn-conditioned statement that Search draws one fewer card conveys the ordinary three-to-two implication and the exclusion of a remote Search triggered solely by rule; no separate arithmetic recital or separately worded “no” is required when those meanings are clear. Explicit contrary rules remain errors.

questions.question: When may Great Slum discard a card first, and does this allow discarding there at any unrelated time?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: When playing or moving a card to this site,may first discard card there,subject locks. It is a timed permission,not unrestricted discard at other times.
questions.source_references: Site Reference p2 Great Slum; Law 7.2.2

required_facts.expected_fact: When playing/moving a card there, may first discard a card there, respecting locks.
No unrestricted discard at other times.

questions.question: Who chooses destination when traveling from enemy-ruled Shrouded Wood, what is its fixed cost, and does forced banishment bypass it?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Fixed cost two before other Travel modifiers;ignore Narrow Pass/Hidden Place. If enemy rules it,travel to ruler choice (Chancellor for Empire),even when another player forces travel. Banishment spends no Supply but does not override destination choice.
questions.source_references: Site Reference p2 Shrouded Wood; Law 5.5.7.III; Errata 5.6

required_facts.expected_fact: Travel from enemy-ruled Shrouded Wood goes to ruler’s choice; Chancellor chooses for Empire.
Two before other Travel modifiers.
Does not override ruler’s destination choice; banishment spends no Supply.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Shrouded Wood ignores Narrow Pass/Hidden Place.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Route-entry exceptions are not asked by destination chooser, cost and forced-choice clauses.

questions.question: Do Plains and Mountain modify dice only if the site itself is targeted, and does ruling the site cancel the modifier?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Mandatory +one attack die Plains/−one Mountain if any targets at site,including site,even if attacker rules it. Not dependent on site being target itself.

required_facts.expected_fact: Mandatory +1 attack die Plains/−1 Mountain for any target at that site, even if attacker rules it.
Site itself need not be a target.

questions.question: What additional warband does River grant, and what happens if you Muster there without ruling it?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: If Muster at River and rule it,gain one more warband,three total ordinary. If do not rule it,ordinary two;eligible empty card,cost still applies and finite bank limit.

required_facts.expected_fact: Muster at River while ruling gives one additional warband (ordinary total three).
Without rule gain ordinary two.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Usual empty-card cost and finite-bank limitation.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Baseline Muster eligibility/source rule is context, not River’s requested additional/no-rule effect.

questions.question: Traveling from Charming Valley in Provinces normally costs how much Supply? What if a spend-no-Supply power is used?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Base two plus one increase=three. Spend-no-Supply overrides increase,zero Supply. Fixed-number change applied before increases.
questions.source_references: Site Reference p2 Charming Valley; Law 7.6.2; Errata 5.6

required_facts.expected_fact: Two base plus one increase equals three Supply.
Overrides increase for zero payment.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: No fixed-number modifier is in the stated arithmetic; general hierarchy is context, not a new recital.

numeric_application.given_state: Travel from Charming Valley in Provinces; a power says to spend no Supply.
numeric_application.completed_events: Apply the site’s +1 Travel modifier, then the final free-Travel override.
numeric_application.calculation: 2 base Supply + 1 = 3; final override sets payment to 0.
numeric_application.numeric_result: Adjusted cost is 3 Supply; actual payment is 0 Supply.

numeric_application.given_state: Travel from Charming Valley while in Provinces, to another region; an applicable spend-no-Supply power is also considered.
numeric_application.completed_events: Base Provinces-to-Hinterland Travel is 2 Supply; Charming Valley increases Travel cost by 1. Free Travel then overrides payment.
numeric_application.calculation: 2 + 1 = 3 Supply before Free Travel; final payment with Free Travel = 0.
numeric_application.numeric_result: 3 Supply normally; 0 if Free Travel applies.

questions.question: Who may use Tribunal’s Action, what immediate resources does it let players exchange, and how is a disputed future breach resolved?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Its ruler or player whose pawn there may negotiate binding exchange of favor/secrets now,and future actions in combination with any player. Coin flip if unclear whether agreed future promise broken. Does not grant generic immediate exchange of relics/banners.

required_facts.expected_fact: Ruler or player whose pawn is there.
Binding immediate favor/secrets and future actions with any player; not generic immediate relic/banner transfers.
Coin flip if unclear whether broken.

questions.question: How does Bandit Crown affect empty sites, picking up last physical warband, defense and sacrificing bandits?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Treat bandits as own warbands:rule empty faceup sites,may pick up last physical at own site,add bandits at targeted sites to defense or relevant attack with powers. Bandits cannot kill/move/sacrifice for skulls,losses,Tyrant/Cursed Cauldron.

required_facts.expected_fact: Treat bandits as own warbands, rule empty faceup sites, may pick up last physical own-site warband.
Add bandits at targeted sites to defense.
Bandits cannot be killed/moved/sacrificed, including loss/skull/payment attempts.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Relevant attacking-force bandits through powers; Tyrant/Cursed Cauldron names.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Attack use and named examples are context; requested defense and inability to sacrifice must be correct without listing every card.

questions.question: Can a player rule a facedown site or put cards there using a move power? What does a ruined edifice contribute to capacity, suit and action access?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: No:only faceup sites ruled and facedown sites cannot hold cards. Ruin counts denizen/edifice capacity,has no suit,cannot Muster/Trade,but its power still functions per access/text.

required_facts.expected_fact: Cannot rule facedown site; only faceup rule. Facedown site cannot hold cards even via move power.
Counts site denizen/edifice capacity, no suit, cannot Muster/Trade.
Ruin power still functions subject to access/text.

questions.question: Must every draw from the world deck follow the entire Search draw-stop procedure, or does the corrected Draw glossary differ? What always happens when a Vision is drawn from world deck?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Corrected Draw simply takes top cards from prompted source;does not automatically import all Search rules into other powers. Always advance Visions Drawn for world-deck Vision,including Oracle. Search itself must stop at world Vision.

required_facts.expected_fact: Draw means take top cards from prompted source; does not import entire Search procedure into other powers.
Always advance Visions Drawn when a world-deck Vision drawn; Search itself stops at its first Vision.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Universal rule includes Oracle; no separate proper-name requirement.

questions.question: Can you take several major/minor actions in any order, stop without spending all Supply, or begin another action before current one finishes?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Any number/order/repeats including none while costs payable;may stop and preserve unspent Supply through Rest;must finish current action before next. No interrupting Campaign with another normal minor action.

required_facts.expected_fact: Any number/order/repeats including none while costs payable; may stop and preserve unspent Supply via Rest.
Must finish current action before another normal major/minor action.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Covered by general no-overlapping-actions rule; no extra example wording required.

questions.question: If you seize a banner by Conspiracy or a binding transfer rather than Campaign, does it lose resources? How does Recover differ?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Any taking except Recover is seizure;burn two banner favor/secrets down to minimum one,People’s Favor Mob. Recover instead replaces resources with paid outbid,distributes old as described,and People’s Favor normal. No burn-two seizure on Recover.

required_facts.expected_fact: Any taking except Recover is seizure, including Conspiracy/binding transfer; burn two banner resources to minimum one, People’s Favor Mob.
Recover pays strictly higher bid, replaces stack with payment and redistributes old resources, People’s Favor normal; no burn-two seizure penalty.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Full old-resource distribution sequence and personal secret split.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: This contrast question is not a second full Recover procedure; broad replacement/redistribution contrast suffices without repeating Q012’s complete bank-order mechanics.

questions.question: Can a Citizen’s defensive battle plan prohibit other Allies’ battle plans, and who decides contested order or competing use of a shared plan?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Power references you/defender cover whole defending side,so cannot-use-other-plans limits all Allies. Your site/board remain individual. Declared defender resolves order/priority and competing shared use;one specific plan once total,user pays.

required_facts.expected_fact: Side-wide you/defender wording means cannot-use-other-plans restriction applies to whole defending side.
Declared defender decides contested order/priority and who uses a shared plan.
Specific plan once total; chosen user pays.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Location/board exception is not implicated in the asked plan prohibition or disputed-order question.

questions.question: When a new Citizen’s conversion needs more purple warbands than available, who decides what is removed, and what is converted when that Citizen later becomes Exile?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: New Citizen chooses which existing board/map warbands to replace purple and which to remove for shortage. Later exile converts only board warbands to own color;map garrisons stay purple. Gain/take source shortage maximum possible.

required_facts.expected_fact: New Citizen chooses existing board/map warbands to replace with available purple and which to remove.
Only board warbands change to own color; map garrisons stay purple.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Availability limit is already operational in shortage conversion; not a separate generic-rule recital.

questions.question: If the People’s Favor is normal with five favor and its holder adds one at Wake, how many choices happen this Wake? What if it was already Mob?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Normal begins with one choice;add sixth then final check flips Mob,no retroactive second choice. Already Mob makes two choices,each obeying last-favor restriction;does not revert just by falling below six.

required_facts.expected_fact: One choice, sixth added, final flip Mob with no retroactive second choice.
Two choices; Mob does not automatically revert below six.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Given starting five and at most two choices, last favor cannot be reached; general limit is contextual to this numerical scenario.

numeric_application.given_state: People’s Favor is on its normal side with five favor; holder adds one during Wake.
numeric_application.completed_events: Make the normal-side choice, then check the Mob threshold; separately compare an already-Mob banner’s two choices.
numeric_application.numeric_result: One choice occurs this Wake and the banner flips to Mob afterward. If already Mob at the start of Wake, make two choices.

reader-b.case_result: At five favor on normal-side People’s Favor, adding one is the single normal-side choice; Mob is checked afterward and flips at six, without a retroactive second choice. If already Mob at Wake start, repeat the choice once, for two choices.

shared_values: Absence alone is not penalized; any volunteered materially false ruling is still incorrect.
Assess the stated requested rule in context; no exact-keyword demand, confidence-label grading, or borrowing from another answer.
